# Benchmark — Shield

**Generated by `npm run benchmark`. Do not edit by hand.**

Measures SIH metric 2 (recall and precision of PII detection) and metric 3 (precision of redaction) against a hand-labelled corpus. Labels describe the PAGE, never the detector output — several are things the DOM path structurally cannot see, and they are counted as misses because they are.

Last run: 2026-09-09T16:03:37.566Z

## Headline

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Pages | 38 |
| Sensitive elements labelled | 150 |
| **Recall** | **81.3%** |
| **Precision** | **83.0%** |
| F1 | 82.2% |
| Category accuracy | 88.5% |
| Missed | 28 |
| Over-flagged | 25 |
| Redaction coverage | 56.5% |
| **Redaction precision** | **83.4%** |
| Area painted / area needed | 0.68x |

Coverage is the share of sensitive AREA painted — but a blanket blur also scores 100% there, so it is never quoted alone. **Redaction precision** is what metric 3 asks: of everything covered, how much needed covering. A blanket blur scores near zero. The area ratio is signed — above 1.00x means more was painted than needed, below means some was left visible.

## Where the pages come from

| Source | Pages | What that means |
|---|---|---|
| synthetic | 32 | Written from what a real page of that kind carries, in the field-naming conventions those portals use - but authored here. |
| fixture | 6 | Test screens, written to exercise our own code. |

**No page in this corpus was written by anybody outside this project.** Every number above is a measurement against our own description of what these pages contain. That is a real limit on what they prove, it is the reason this column is printed, and closing it is the remaining half of TASKS.md T1.1.

## The pixel layer

What is printed inside an image, scored against boxes measured on the document rather than against element labels. An element label cannot express this: the element is the whole card, so it cannot tell covering the number apart from painting over the entire image, and that difference is what metric 3 asks about.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Documents scored | 2 |
| Regions labelled | 11 |
| Recall | 27.3% |
| Precision | 100.0% |
| Category accuracy | 100.0% |
| Coverage | 40.9% |
| Redaction precision | 64.3% |

A match needs an intersection-over-union of 0.5 against the labelled box, so a rectangle covering the whole card does not count as having found the number on it.

**This is not a measurement of the recognition engine.** Tesseract needs a browser and cannot run here, so the words above are perfect readings of the committed sample documents. What is measured is everything after the engine - line grouping, the shared classifier, box placement - which lives in this repository and had no measurement at all.

Labelled in pixels and not yet measured:

- `05-adversarial` - 1 box(es), no reading available.

Faces carry no boxes here at all. `test-screens/face-a.jpg` and `face-b.png` are deliberately not committed, so a face box would depend on photographs this repository does not contain. Inventing one would be making up the only number in the file nobody could check. Face detection is measured in Chrome and recorded in TASKS.md: 6 of 8, reliable at 110px and above.

## What this does not measure

- **OCR, faces and the visual layer.** They need a browser and pixel ground truth, not element labels. Any identifier reachable only through pixels appears here as a miss.
- **Extraction.** `dom-map.ts` needs real layout and a real browser. The element maps here are hand-derived from the fixture markup.
- **Generalisation.** The corpus source column says how much of this is our own fixtures. Growing the `real` share is TASKS.md T1.1.
